claim: Jacobs replaced the incumbent operator and implemented CMMS- and PdM-based maintenance programs on two named prior projects (Vancouver, WA and Waterbury, CT)
Reporting gap under the incumbent is documented as four missing evidence categories: PM/PdM findings, failure mode/FMEA use, trend and asset-health analysis, and completed corrective actions
Every work order is documented with field evidence — photos, parts usage, meter readings — plus supervisor verification and timely closeout
unit: required field evidence types per work order

claim: Real-time dashboards shared with the client show PM compliance, CM backlog, labor, cost, and asset health
Maintenance program is built on an Asset Management System aligned to ISO 55001
Governance is one Maintenance Committee supported by two subcommittees (CMMS and SCADA)
Jacobs' AMS framework has 10 elements, based on the IAM 10-Box Excellence Model and consistent with Global Forum on Maintenance and Asset Management guidance
PM Optimization reviews frequencies, failure modes, and job plans at least annually
Asset registry validation and QR/barcode tagging using a CMMS-aligned data dictionary are completed during mobilization
Improvement cadence is monthly KPI reviews with the Maintenance Committee, quarterly PMO checkpoints, annual internal audits by dedicated technical experts, and after-action reviews for major events
Client has live dashboard access to six maintenance KPIs: PM compliance, CM backlog and aging, MTBF/MTTR, asset availability, labor/parts cost, and evidence lag (time to close with proof)
A CMMS Champion is provided on each maintenance crew to coach mobile use and data quality, alongside one dedicated Planner/Scheduler
unit: CMMS Champion per crew; 1 dedicated Planner/Scheduler

claim: AMS spans four asset domains — WRF process units, conveyance/tunnels and structures, facilities, and fleet — with NEXGEN EAM as the system of record integrated to SCADA/Historian and GIS
unit: asset domains in a single view

claim: Work order life cycle has five stages: creation, planning and preparation, execution, verification and closure, and chronic issue management
The Planner/Scheduler builds a two-week schedule through work list review
Integrated reliability-focused maintenance program rests on six key items for success, including managing CM/PM backlog as a leading risk indicator
Facility-specific reliability enhancement plans for both water reclamation facilities were already developed before award, from review of the client's O&M manuals and the RFP scope
Cogeneration reliability plan focuses on three practical levers: make data actionable, make alarms meaningful, and prevent repeat shutdowns through disciplined root cause analysis and closure
Cogeneration reliability plan covers five uptime-critical systems: fuel gas conditioning and compression, cooling water, fuel quality, turbine operating envelope, and waste heat
Alarms are tiered into four levels — information, warning, critical, and safety shutdown — with clear response and escalation expectations
Reliability governance closure cadence is weekly reliability huddles and monthly leadership reviews

Second WRF cogeneration plan targets four common reliability constraints: digester gas variability and siloxane breakthrough, compressor fuel pressure instability, seasonal cooling water imbalances, and hot water loop interactions affecting jacket water temperature stability
Second WRF cogeneration fleet comprises Caterpillar units plus one White Superior engine
unit: White Superior engine (plus multiple Caterpillar units)

claim: Unified health dashboard provides four indices operators can act on: gas compression, fuel quality, cooling water, and hot water
